questions.question: What is the capacity of new StringBuilder() with no arguments?
questions.explanation: An empty builder starts with room for 16 characters. Its length() is still 0.

questions.question: A StringBuilder with capacity 34 is full and one more character is appended. What is the new capacity?
StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder("OTP"); sb.append(42).insert(0, "#"); System.out.println(sb); What is printed?
questions.explanation: append adds 42 at the end, giving OTP42, then insert(0, "#") puts # at the front.

questions.question: StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder("Running late"); sb.delete(0, 8); System.out.println(sb); What is printed?
questions.explanation: delete(0, 8) removes indexes 0 to 7: the seven letters of Running plus the space, leaving late.

questions.question: StringBuilder a = new StringBuilder("hi"); StringBuilder b = new StringBuilder("hi"); System.out.println(a.equals(b)); What is printed?
questions.explanation: StringBuilder does not override equals, so it compares references. Two separate builders are never equal.

questions.question: Two threads append log lines to one shared StringBuilder at the same time. What is the risk?
options: Lines can be lost or mixed because StringBuilder is not synchronized
questions.explanation: Use StringBuffer or separate builders per thread when more than one thread writes.

questions.question: String report = ""; for (String line : lines) { report += line; } runs over 50,000 lines. What is the problem?
options: Each += creates a new String and copies all text so far, which is slow
questions.explanation: Repeated copying makes the work grow with the square of the length. Build it with one StringBuilder instead.

questions.question: Why can calls like sb.append("a").append("b") be chained?
options: append returns the same StringBuilder object
questions.explanation: Most editing methods return this, the same builder, so the next call runs on the same object.

questions.question: StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder("Hello"); System.out.println(sb.length() + " " + sb.capacity()); What is printed?
questions.explanation: The builder holds 5 characters, and its capacity is the string length plus 16, which is 21.

questions.question: Which statement about StringBuilder and StringBuffer is correct?
options: StringBuilder is not synchronized, so it is faster for use by one thread
Only StringBuffer has a reverse() method
questions.explanation: Both are mutable and share the same methods. StringBuffer locks each call; StringBuilder, added in Java 5, does not.
